Every operating room,open to every trainee.

Live surgery, a video library, 3D case prep and an AI study companion, through the surgeon’s eyes.

Prototype · sample content
The problem

Trainees can only see what the surgical team lets them see. They stand outside the sterile field, behind the team, and learn from whatever cases their own hospital happens to get.

The education gap

What learning from the back of the room costs.

// In the roomOR sightline simulation
0%

of the incision is in a resident’s direct line of sight from behind the attending, who sees 96%. From our simulation, not a clinical measurement.

// CostLeoni et al., Va J Med, 2026
54.9%

of fourth-year medical students declined an away rotation because of cost.

The platform

One camera in the OR. Six ways to learn from it.

Who it’s for

Built for trainees. Useful to the surgeons who teach them.

Residency programs and medical schools give their trainees the cases their own operating rooms cannot.

For medical students

100,723

Real operating-room exposure before clinical years, and a way to explore specialties without the cost of travel.

For surgical residents

29,000

Cases beyond their own hospital’s schedule, with 3D prep and cited answers for the night before.

For attending surgeons

155,000

Teaching reach past their own OR. Their technique follows their career, not one hospital.

US counts: AAMC 2025–26 MD enrollment; American College of Surgeons Bulletin, Jul/Aug 2025.

The view from the surgeon’s eyes

The feed shows the operative field itself, not the backs of the team.

Case prep in 3D

The target, the approach and the structures at risk, in front of the team before the case starts.

Made for people still learning

Trending techniques and Ask Surgeonary are built for trainees, not adapted from another tool.
